entry.title: Harmonised standards for free: where to read them, and how to comment on the drafts
entry.summary: Harmonised standards cited in the Official Journal can be read free of charge on the portals of the national standardisation bodies; drafts only during the public enquiry. A country-by-country list, what it means for the Cyber Resilience Act standards, and what the proposed new Standardisation Regulation would change.

entry.title: Where ENISA consults: ten channels, two feeds, and drafts that are announced elsewhere
entry.summary: ENISA does not publish more than it did in 2023, but in more places and by more rules. Its certification work consults in an orderly way on its own website. Its guidance for manufacturers under the Cyber Resilience Act was put out for comment in 2026 as PDF files on its server, mostly without a news item on its site, and became known through LinkedIn and community mailing lists. The Cybersecurity Act 2 would make such guidance a standing task of ENISA, so far without a duty to consult on it.

entry.title: NIS-2 amendment: EP committee vote close to the end of its window
entry.summary: The forecast expects it around 1 Feb 2027. It keeps its median of publication only if the step comes by 16 Dec 2026; on 17 Nov 2026 that left 29 days. Until 16 Dec 2026 the median of publication in the Official Journal stays within 14 days of 25 Aug 2027, the median of 25 Mar 2026, when the procedure reached its current step; later, it moves later with every week. If the step came on 17 Nov 2026, the median would be 31 Jul 2027.

entry.title: EU Space Act: EP committee vote reached after its window
entry.summary: EP committee vote on 19 Nov 2026, 101 days after the window (until 10 Aug 2026). The step came after its window: the median of publication had moved later by then; the forecast now starts from the next step. On 8 Sep 2025, when the procedure reached its previous step, the median of publication in the Official Journal was 13 Aug 2027; since 19 Nov 2026 it is 4 Dec 2027.
